column1: # tools/ledger_overrides.tsv -- a verdict row's description where the commit
# that closed the verdict was subjected outside `tools/ledger.py`'s subject
# rule. S334.
# The rule reads a row's run and description from the closing commit's
# subject, and history is never rewritten, so a subject in the wrong form
# reads out wrong at every regeneration. A row here replaces that commit's
# description and nothing else; the run, the numbers and the class still come
# from its result block. Written as the table's other rows read.
# Columns. `sha` is the closing commit's full sha, `git log --format=%H`: an
# abbreviation is unique only in the history it was taken from. `what` is the
# description the row prints. `by` is the step or decision that recorded it.
# `tools/ledger.py` refuses to print on a short or repeated sha, an empty
# `what` or one carrying `|`, a `by` that is no S<nnn> or DEC-<nnn>, a sha that
# closes no verdict the ledger prints, and a sha whose subject already reads
# out cleanly under the rule -- so a row cannot restyle a clean subject, and
# the file holds only commits that need it. Its header lists the same.
# 1ffc96e, S122's H1, was subjected "Ship S122's fitted king safety family on
# its H1 (S122, DEC-353)" and read "Ship 's fitted king safety family on its
# H1 (S122, DEC-353)"; its neighbours read "the passed pawn family", "the pawn
# structure family", "the threat family".
